<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">FOREST LABORATORIES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">(continued)</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
&#160;</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Forest has reached settlements in the Alabama, Alaska, Hawaii, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, and Oklahoma actions, as well as all of the actions brought by the New York counties in federal and state court, as well as the action brought by the State of Mississippi on behalf of the State and School Employees&#8217; Life and Health Insurance plan.&#160;&#160;Forest has also settled with the State of Texas before the commencement of a lawsuit.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s settlement payments are not material to its financial condition or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Forest remains a defendant in the Illinois, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Utah actions, as well as the Wisconsin qui tam action.&#160;&#160;Discovery is ongoing.&#160;&#160;Motions to dismiss with respect to the Illinois, Louisiana, and Mississippi actions were denied.&#160;&#160;The motion to dismiss the Utah action was granted, but the Utah Supreme Court, while upholding the lower court&#8217;s ruling regarding a statute of limitations issue, reversed that ruling and allowed the plaintiff to replead.&#160;&#160;The plaintiff filed another Amended Complaint, and the defendants have filed a motion to dismiss, which will be argued sometime in the next two months.&#160;&#160;The motion to dismiss the Wisconsin qui tam complaint is pending.&#160;&#160;It is not anticipated that any trials involving Forest in these matters will take place before 2014, although technically all of the brand companies are potentially subject to a November 2013 trial date in Louisiana.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FLI and FPI are defendants in three federal actions filed on behalf of individuals who purchased Celexa or Lexapro for pediatric use, all of which have been consolidated for pretrial purposes in a multi-district litigation (MDL) proceeding in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts under the caption <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;In re Celexa and Lexapro Marketing and Sales Practices Litigation.&#8221;</font>&#160;&#160;These actions, two of which were originally filed as purported nationwide class actions, and one of which is a purported California-wide class action, allege that FLI and FPI marketed Celexa and/or Lexapro for off-label pediatric use and paid illegal kickbacks to physicians to induce prescriptions of Celexa and Lexapro.&#160;&#160;The complaints assert various similar claims, including claims under the Missouri consumer protection statute and state common laws.&#160;&#160;On February 5, 2013, the district judge overseeing the MDL denied all plaintiffs&#8217; motions for class certification.&#160;&#160;On February 18, 2013, the plaintiff in the California action filed a petition seeking leave to appeal this decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit.&#160;&#160;On April 16, 2013, the First Circuit denied the petition.&#160; On April 30, 2013, plaintiffs in the other two actions filed amended complaints seeking to certify state-wide class actions in Illinois, Missouri, and New York under those states&#8217; consumer protection statutes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 3, 2013, an action was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California seeking to certify a state-wide class action in California and alleging that FLI and FPI&#8217;s promotion of Lexapro for adolescent depression was deceptive.&#160;&#160;Plaintiffs&#8217; motions for class certification related to these amended complaints are due June 28, 2013.&#160;&#160;FLI and FPI intend to continue to vigorously defend against these cases.&#160;&#160;At this time, the Company believes an unfavorable outcome is less than probable and is unable to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of possible loss, but does not believe losses, if any, would have a material effect on the results of operations or financial position taken as a whole.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FLI and/or FPI are also named as defendants in two similar actions filed on behalf of entities or individuals who purchased or reimbursed certain purchases of Celexa or Lexapro pending in the Missouri Circuit Court, Twenty-Second Judicial Circuit, arising from nearly identical allegations as those contained in the federal actions described in the immediately preceding paragraph.&#160;&#160;The first action, filed on July 22, 2009 under the caption <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;Crawford v. Forest Pharmaceuticals, Inc.,&#8221;</font> and now known as <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;Luster v. Forest Pharmaceuticals, Inc.,&#8221;</font> is a putative class action on behalf of a class of Missouri citizens who purchased Celexa for pediatric use.&#160;&#160;Only FPI, which is headquartered in Missouri, is named as a defendant.&#160;&#160;The complaint asserts claims under the Missouri consumer protection statute and Missouri common law, and seeks unspecified damages and attorneys&#8217; fees.&#160;&#160;In October 2010, the court certified a class of Missouri domiciliary citizens who purchased Celexa for pediatric use at any time prior to the date of the class certification order, but who do not have a claim for personal injury.&#160;&#160;Discovery is currently ongoing.&#160;&#160;The second action, filed on November 6, 2009 under the caption <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;St. Louis Labor Healthcare Network et al. v. Forest Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and Forest Laboratories, Inc.,&#8221;</font> is brought by two entities that purchased or reimbursed certain purchases of Celexa or Lexapro.&#160;&#160;The complaint asserts claims under the Missouri consumer protection statute and Missouri common law, and seeks unspecified damages and attorneys&#8217; fees.&#160;&#160;FLI and FPI intend to continue to vigorously defend against both of these actions.&#160;&#160;At this time, the Company believes an unfavorable outcome is less than probable and is unable to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of possible loss, but does not believe losses, if any, would have a material effect on the results of operations or financial position taken as a whole.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company received a subpoena dated April 20, 2011 from the Office of the U.S. Attorney for the District of Massachusetts.&#160;&#160;The subpoena requests documents relating to Benicar, Benicar HCT (collectively Benicar) and Azor, prescription medications approved for the treatment of hypertension.&#160;&#160;The Company co-marketed Benicar from 2002 to 2008 together with the drug&#8217;s originator Daiichi Sankyo, Inc. pursuant to co-promotion agreements.&#160;&#160;The Company is cooperating in responding to the subpoena.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">FOREST LABORATORIES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">(continued)</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company received a subpoena dated May 6, 2013 from the Office of the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York.&#160;&#160;The subpoena requests documents relating to Tudorza Pressair.&#160;&#160;The Company is cooperating in responding to the subpoena.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company received a subpoena dated January 26, 2006 from the U.S. Attorney&#8217;s Office for the District of Massachusetts requesting documents related to its commercial relationship with Omnicare, Inc. (Omnicare), a long-term care pharmacy provider, including but not limited to documents concerning its contracts with Omnicare, and rebates and other payments made by the Company to Omnicare.&#160;&#160;The Company understands that the subpoena was issued in connection with that office&#8217;s investigation of potential criminal violations of federal healthcare laws by Omnicare and potentially others.&#160;&#160;The Company is cooperating in this investigation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company currently is defending approximately 161 product liability lawsuits.&#160;&#160;Fourteen of the lawsuits allege that Celexa or Lexapro caused or contributed to individuals committing or attempting suicide, or caused a violent event.&#160;&#160;One hundred and forty-six of the lawsuits allege that Celexa or Lexapro caused various birth defects.&#160;&#160;Each lawsuit seeks substantial compensatory and punitive damages.&#160;&#160;The Company is vigorously defending these suits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A MDL was established for the majority of the suicidality-related litigation, with the federal court cases being transferred to Judge Rodney Sippel in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri.&#160;&#160;The remaining twelve cases in the MDL are expected to be remanded in the near future to the federal district courts in which they were filed originally.&#160;&#160;A state court case involving a young woman who allegedly attempted suicide is set for trial in August 2013 in Montgomery, Alabama.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The majority of the various birth defect cases have been consolidated in Cole County Circuit Court in Missouri.&#160;&#160;Sixteen cases have been filed in the Superior Court of New Jersey (ten in Atlantic County and six in Hudson County).&#160;&#160;The New Jersey cases have been removed to the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey.&#160;&#160;The Company expects that the state court consolidation will ease the burden of defending these cases.&#160;&#160;The Company hopes that the consolidated proceedings will promote the economical and efficient resolution of these lawsuits and provide it with a meaningful opportunity to vindicate the Company&#8217;s products.&#160;&#160;However, litigation is inherently subject to uncertainty and the Company cannot predict or determine the outcome of this litigation.&#160;&#160;The Company generally maintains $140 million of product liability coverage (annually, per &#8220;occurrence&#8221; on a claims-made basis, and in the aggregate).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company received two subpoenas dated April 27, 2007 from the Office of the Attorney General of the State of Delaware requesting documents relating to its use of the &#8220;nominal price&#8221; exception to the Medicaid program&#8217;s &#8220;Best Price&#8221; rules.&#160; The Company understands that comparable subpoenas have been or will be issued to other pharmaceutical manufacturers as part of that office&#8217;s investigation of the use of the &#8220;nominal price&#8221; exception.&#160;&#160;The Company has complied with the subpoenas.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In March 2012, the Company and Janssen, its licensor for Bystolic, brought actions for infringement of U.S. Patent No. 6,545,040 (the &#8216;040 patent) in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware and the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois against several companies who have notified them that they have filed Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs) with the FDA seeking to obtain approval to market generic versions of Bystolic before the &#8216;040 patent expires on December 21, 2021.&#160;&#160;These lawsuits triggered an automatic stay of approval of the applicable ANDAs until June 17, 2015 (unless a court issues an adverse decision sooner).&#160;&#160;Janssen is no longer a party to these lawsuits following the Company&#8217;s agreement to buy out Janssen&#8217;s interests in Bystolic.&#160;&#160;On June 12, 2012, the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation centralized the Delaware and Illinois actions in the Northern District of Illinois before Judge Elaine E. Bucklo for coordinated or consolidated pretrial proceedings captioned <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;In re Nebivolol (&#8216;040) Patent Litigation.&#8221;&#160;&#160;</font>Fact discovery is scheduled to be completed by June 8, 2013, and expert discovery is scheduled to be completed by November 22, 2013.&#160;&#160;A claim construction hearing is scheduled for July 26, 2013.&#160;&#160;No trial dates have been set.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">(continued)</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has entered into settlement agreements with four of the six defendant groups in such patent infringement litigation: Hetero Labs Ltd and Hetero USA Inc. (October 2012); Torrent Pharmaceuticals Ltd and Torrent Pharma Inc. (November 2012); Alkem Laboratories Ltd. and Indchemie Health Specialties Pvt. Ltd. (November 2012); and Glenmark Generics Inc., USA, Glenmark Generics Ltd. and Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Ltd (December 2012) (collectively, the &#8220;Settling Defendants&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the settlement agreements, and subject to review of the settlement terms by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, the Company will provide a license to each of the Settling Defendants that will permit them to launch their respective generic versions of Bystolic as of the date that is the later of (a) three calendar months prior to the expiration of the &#8216;040 patent, including any extensions and/or pediatric exclusivities or (b) the date that each Settling Defendant receives final FDA approval of its ANDA, or earlier in certain circumstances.&#160;&#160;The Company also agreed to reimburse certain of the Settling Defendants&#8217; legal costs in connection with the patent litigation, which were not material.&#160;&#160;These settlement agreements do not settle the Company&#8217;s patent infringement litigations against the other generic manufacturers that are also part of <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">In re Nebivolol</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">(&#8216;040)</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Patent Litigation</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2012, the Company was named as a defendant (along with FPI) in an action brought by Megan Barrett, Lindsey Houser, Jennifer Jones, and Jennifer Seard, former Company Sales Representatives, in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York under the caption <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;Megan Barrett et al. v. Forest Laboratories Inc. and Forest Pharmaceuticals, Inc.&#8221;</font>&#160;&#160;In November 2012, Plaintiffs amended the complaint, adding six additional plaintiffs: Kimberly Clinton, Erin Eckenrode, Julie Smyth, Marie Avila, Andrea Harley, and Christy Lowder, all of whom alleged that they are current or former Company Sales Representatives or Specialty Sales Representatives.&#160; In March 2013, Plaintiffs filed a second amended complaint, adding one additional plaintiff: Tracy Le, a current Company Sales Representative.&#160; The action is a putative class and collective action, and the second amended complaint alleges class claims under Title VII for gender discrimination with respect to pay and promotions, as well as discrimination on the basis of pregnancy, and a collective action claim under the Equal Pay Act.&#160;&#160;The proposed Title VII gender class includes all current and former female Sales Representatives (defined to include Territory Sales Representatives, Field Sales Representatives, Medical Sales Representatives, Professional Sales Representatives, Specialty Sales Representatives, Field Sales Trainers, and Regional Sales Trainers) employed by the Company throughout the U.S. from 2008 to the date of judgment, and the proposed Title VII pregnancy sub-class includes all current and former female Sales Representatives who have been, are, or will become pregnant while employed by the Company throughout the U.S. from 2008 to the date of judgment.&#160;&#160;The proposed Equal Pay Act collective action class includes current, former, and future female Sales Representatives who were not compensated equally to similarly-situated male employees during the applicable liability period.&#160;&#160;The second amended complaint also includes non-class claims on behalf of certain of the named Plaintiffs for sexual harassment and retaliation under Title VII, and for violations of the Family and Medical Leave Act.&#160;&#160;The Company filed a motion to dismiss certain claims on April 29, 2013.&#160; The Company believes there is no merit to Plaintiffs&#8217; claims and intends to vigorously defend this lawsuit.&#160;&#160;At this time, the Company believes an unfavorable outcome is less than probable and is unable to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of possible loss, but does not believe losses, if any, would have a material effect on the results of operations or financial position taken as a whole.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is also subject to various legal proceedings that arise from time to time in the ordinary course of its business.&#160;&#160;Although the Company believes that the proceedings brought against it, including the product liability cases described above, are without merit and the Company has product liability and other insurance, litigation is subject to many factors which are difficult to predict and there can be no assurance that the Company will not incur material costs in the resolution of these matters.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has federal, state and local net operating loss carryforwards as well as excess charitable contribution carryovers which are available to reduce future U.S. federal and state taxable income, expiring at various times between 2013 and 2029.&#160;&#160;Although not material, valuation allowances have been established for a portion of deferred tax assets acquired as part of the Cerexa purchase as the Company determined that it was more likely than not that these benefits will not be realized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At March 31, 2013, U.S. taxes have not been provided on approximately $6.3 billion of undistributed earnings of foreign subsidiaries as these undistributed earnings are indefinitely reinvested offshore.&#160;&#160;If, in the future, these earnings are repatriated to the U.S., or if such earnings are expected to be remitted in the foreseeable future, additional tax provisions would be required.&#160;&#160;Due to complexities in the tax laws and the assumptions that would have to be made, it is not practicable to estimate the amounts of income taxes that would have to be provided.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company accrues liabilities for identified tax contingencies that result from positions that are being challenged or could be challenged by tax authorities.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that its accrual for tax liabilities is adequate for all open years, based on Management&#8217;s assessment of many factors, including its interpretations of the tax law and judgments about potential actions by tax authorities.&#160;&#160;However, it is possible that the ultimate resolution of any tax audit may be materially greater or lower than the amount accrued.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s income tax returns for fiscal years prior to 2003 in most jurisdictions and prior to 2007 in Ireland are no longer subject to review as such fiscal years are generally closed.&#160;&#160;Tax authorities in various jurisdictions are in the process of reviewing the Company&#8217;s income tax returns for various post-2002 fiscal years, including the Internal Revenue Service.&#160;&#160;The Company has received a preliminary transfer pricing assessment from the IRS for fiscal years 2004, 2005 and 2006 and the matter likely will be settled within the next 12 months.&#160;&#160;If the Company were to agree to this preliminary assessment it would be within previously established tax reserves.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company and Almirall, S.A. (Almirall) received FDA approval for Tudorza<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"> TM</font> Pressair<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"> TM</font> in July 2012, for the long-term maintenance treatment of bronchospasm associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, including chronic bronchitis and emphysema.&#160;&#160;The Company licensed rights to aclidinium in the U.S. through an agreement with Almirall pursuant to which the Company made a milestone payment of $40 million which was due upon FDA approval.&#160; The milestone payment was capitalized as an intangible asset and will be amortized over the life of the patent for Tudorza Pressair.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 14, 2012, the Company announced an agreement with Adamas Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Adamas) for the development and commercialization of a fixed dose combination (FDC) of Namenda XR <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">TM</font> (memantine HCl extended release) and donepezil HCl which will be a daily therapy for the treatment of moderate to severe dementia of the Alzheimer&#8217;s type.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the agreement, the Company made an upfront payment of $65 million during the quarter ended December 31, 2012 which was recorded in R&amp;D expense.&#160;&#160;The Company may be obligated to pay up to $95 million in future milestones if development and commercialization efforts are successful.&#160;&#160;The Company will have exclusive commercialization rights for this FDC in the U.S.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 1, 2012, the Company announced an agreement with Nabriva for the development of Nabriva&#8217;s novel antibacterial agent, BC-3781.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the agreement, the Company provided funding of $25 million to Nabriva during July 2012, and will conduct, in collaboration with Nabriva, certain development activities related to BC-3781 over the twelve month period following the execution of the agreement.&#160;&#160;During the twelve-month period, the Company has the exclusive right to acquire Nabriva.&#160;&#160;The Company's decision to acquire Nabriva will be dependent upon certain contingencies.&#160;&#160;The Company recorded an asset of $25 million in connection with this agreement which is included within the &#8216;Other assets&#8217; caption in the Balance Sheet.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Ironwood collaboration agreement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September 2007, the Company entered into a collaboration agreement with Ironwood to jointly develop and commercialize Linzess <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">TM</font> for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) and chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC). Under the terms of the Ironwood collaboration agreement, the Company shares equally with Ironwood all profits and losses from the development and sale of linaclotide in the U.S. In addition, Forest obtained exclusive rights to the linaclotide license in Canada and Mexico, for which the Company will pay royalties to Ironwood based on net sales, subject to receiving regulatory approval.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company made non-refundable, up-front payments totaling $70&#160;million to Ironwood.&#160;&#160;The agreement also included contingent milestone payments as well as a contingent equity investment based on&#160;the achievement of specific clinical and commercial milestones.&#160;&#160;As of March 31, 2013, payments totaling $230 million, relating mostly to development milestones, have been made.&#160;&#160;The Company may be obligated to pay up to an additional $100 million if certain sales milestones are achieved.&#160;&#160;The contingent equity investment required the Company to purchase $25 million of Ironwood's convertible preferred stock when a specific clinical milestone was met. This investment is classified within long-term marketable securities and&#160;recorded at fair value. The fair value of the investment at March 31, 2013 is $38.1 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In August 2012, the FDA approved Linzess as a once-daily treatment for adult men and women suffering from IBS-C or CIC.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the Ironwood collaboration agreement, the Company made a milestone payment of $85 million to Ironwood which was due upon FDA approval.&#160;&#160;The milestone payment was capitalized as an intangible asset and will be amortized over the life of the patent for Linzess.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the year ended March 31, 2013, Linzess sales in the U.S. totaled $23.7 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">17.&#160;&#160;Business combinations:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On April 13, 2011, the Company acquired Clinical Data, a specialty pharmaceutical company, for $30 per share, plus contingent consideration, per a Contingent Value Rights agreement (CVR) of up to $6 per share if certain milestones connected to sales of Viibryd, one of the acquired products, are achieved.&#160;&#160;The acquisition was consummated by a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company through a tender offer and merger, pursuant to which the Company acquired all of the outstanding shares of common stock of Clinical Data and all related securities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company fully integrated the operations of Clinical Data into its existing structure.&#160;&#160;The aggregate consideration paid was approximately $1.3 billion, which the Company financed with existing cash.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 36pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Acquired goodwill included the combined synergies of the purchased business, the assembled workforce and the broadening of the Company&#8217;s antidepressant portfolio, a therapeutic area in which the Company has extensive experience.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 36pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In Viibryd, the Company obtained a newly approved product that joined the Company&#8217;s portfolio of products, and which contributed to offsetting the expiration of the patent for Lexapro.&#160;&#160;Sales of Lexapro accounted for approximately 48% of the Company&#8217;s net sales in fiscal 2012.&#160;&#160;Lexapro faced generic competition as a result of its patent expiration in March 2012.&#160;&#160;Sales of Lexapro accounted for approximately 7% of the Company&#8217;s net sales in fiscal 2013.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company gained access to Clinical Data&#8217;s earlier stage development projects in various therapeutic areas.&#160;&#160;The intangible asset recorded at acquisition relates to Viibryd, which will be amortized over 12 years reflecting the life of a patent that covers Viibryd that expires in fiscal 2023.&#160;&#160;None of the goodwill was deductible for tax purposes.&#160;&#160;The carrying amount of the goodwill at the end of the fiscal 2013 was $698.1 million.</font><br>
